title: Assorted Entanglements
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Iori Tanaka, a 28-year-old office worker with a habit of dating married men, drinks too much and wakes up naked beside Minami, a tattooed, pierced bar worker who does not want to forget their night. The series follows their mismatched relationship and several other women's love stories, including Minami's foster sister and Iori's younger sister (AniList; MU; Okazu review).
life_message: Love can grow between unlikely people, and found family can steady those who have had rough starts.

content.note: Slapstick, e.g. Minami's foster sister greets her with a physical attack (Okazu; MU Slapstick Comedy).
Adult women's same-sex relationships; opens with a drunken one-night stand implied, 'light nudity, nothing salacious' (Okazu; AniList; MU). Affairs with married men (AniList; MU Affair/s).
Iori is a 'sloppy drunk' (Okazu); MU Alcoholic, Bar/s.
MU lists Abusive Parent/s and Domestic Abuse in backstories; Minami had 'rough spots' (Okazu).
Heavy drinking and affairs with married men shown as part of Iori's life (AniList; Okazu).
Began as a web manga on Twitter and Pixiv (AniList).

dominant: Adult yuri romance; unlikely couples; found family

frames.aligns: Care between Minami and her foster family.
frames.concerns: Same-sex relationships, a one-night stand and affairs with married men.
Same-sex romance as the core; alcohol.
LCMS/WELS: same-sex romance; ELCA less concerned.

frames.aligns: Hospitality to people with hard histories.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Characters follow their own romantic choices (AniList; MU).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Foster sister and younger sister as found and chosen family (Okazu).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Office worker and bar server as equals (Okazu).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern urban life, no faith elements (MU).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Love and identity as core themes (MU Yuri).

folkways.japan: Reflects Japanese office-worker (OL) life and izakaya drinking culture, described as setting.

delivery.evidence: Okazu calls it 'a goofy manga that requires no deep emotional investment'.
delivery.note: Values arrive through slice-of-life comedy rather than statements.

winners_losers: The unlikely couples get the sympathy; 'a terrible couple that kind of works anyway' (Okazu).
to_verify: Ages of all characters; AniList School tag (60) and MU Delinquent/s suggest a younger character, possibly a minor, in a later arc.
Level of sexual content in later volumes (review covers volume 1 only).
